chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said: I heard my father saying:
Regarding a man who puts on his clothes and prepares for the Ihram, then has intercourse with his wife before he pronounces the Talbiyah for the Ihram, he said: 'Upon him is a Dam (sacrifice).'

This is applicable to the one who did not proclaim the Talbiyah aloud, even if he had contracted his Ihram between himself and his soul, for whenever the matter is as we described, that obligation falls upon him because his Ihram has been contracted.
And that which indicates that if his intercourse is after the Talbiyah and before the Standing (at Arafat), the expiation and repeating the Hajj fall upon him, is what has been narrated:

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation for a ritual breach
key_terms.الْوُقُوفُ: The Standing at Arafat, a pivotal ritual of Hajj
key_terms.تَلْبِيَةٌ: The verbal declaration of entering the state of Ihram (Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk)
key_terms.دَمٌ: A sacrificial animal (usually a sheep or goat) offered as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who has sexual intercourse before or after entering the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the liability of 'Dam' applies even to a private, non-verbal Ihram contract if intercourse occurs before the formal Talbiyah, whereas intercourse after the Talbiyah but before Arafat necessitates a heavier expiation and Hajj repetition. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the moment of verbal declaration (Talbiyah) as the critical threshold for binding the pilgrim to the full legal consequences of Ihram. The ruling underscores the principle that the severity of the penalty correlates with the proximity to the core rituals of Hajj.
